ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a regular hexagon, and the inner central region is shaded gray. Near each vertex of the hexagon there is an unshaded circular sector region; the two radii of the sector lie along adjacent sides of the hexagon, and the arc bends toward the interior of the hexagon; the gray region is exactly the part remaining after removing these six vertex sectors from the interior of the hexagon. Reasoning: The side length of the regular hexagon is 6, and it can be divided into 6 equilateral triangles with side length 6, so the area of the hexagon is 6 × (6^2√3/4) = 54√3. Each interior angle of a regular hexagon is 120°, and the sector radius at each vertex is 3, so the area of each sector is (120/360)π(3^2) = 3π. There are 6 such sectors, with total area 18π. Shaded area = hexagon area - area of six sectors = 54√3 - 18π.

method.method_draft: Use direct complement subtraction. From the image, identify that there are six congruent unshaded circular sectors at the six vertices of the regular hexagon, and the shaded region is exactly the part of the hexagon outside these sectors. From the text, use side length 6 and sector radius 3. Compute the area of the regular hexagon as 6 equilateral triangles of side 6: 6*(36√3/4)=54√3. A regular hexagon has interior angle 120°, so each vertex sector has area (120/360)*π*3^2=3π. There are 6 such sectors, total 18π. Subtract to get shaded area 54√3-18π.

method.method_draft: Use a midpoint-hexagon plus circular-segment correction. From the image, note that each radius-3 arc begins and ends halfway along the two adjacent sides of length 6, so the six arc endpoints are the midpoints of the hexagon sides. Connect these six endpoints mentally to form an inner regular hexagon. The distance between adjacent side midpoints is the chord between two radius-3 points separated by the 120° vertex angle, so its length is 3√3. The inner midpoint hexagon area is (3√3/2)(3√3)^2=81√3/2. However, this straight-edged midpoint hexagon includes six circular segments that are actually unshaded, one at each vertex between the chord and the arc. Each segment equals a 120° sector of radius 3 minus the isosceles triangle with sides 3,3 and included angle 120°: 3π - (1/2)(3)(3)sin120° = 3π - 9√3/4. Subtract six such segments: 81√3/2 - 6(3π - 9√3/4)=54√3-18π.
